topics_checked.note: Federal rules (Immigration Office / IBZ) applied by the commune/gemeente everywhere in Belgium. The DOFI pages (dofi.ibz.be) were behind a captcha, so ibz.be, the EU Immigration Portal and Leuven city pages were used.
Registration is municipal (commune/gemeente) in all three regions; procedures differ slightly per city (Leuven pages read).
National register number (rijksregisternummer / numéro national) vs BIS number. We did not find (or look for) a separate personal tax-ID scheme.
Federal system (mutualité/ziekenfonds, CAAMI-HZIV). Rules for EU students who take a job (when EHIC stops being enough) were not found on an official page.
Only the EU-wide basic payment account right (Your Europe) was found; no Belgian consumer page from FPS Economy turned up (its pages cover businesses only).
Regional operators: De Lijn (Flanders), STIB-MIVB (Brussels), TEC (Wallonia). letec.be refused automated access, so TEC is not covered. Prices are in subsidies.json.
Federal: Student@work (650 hours/calendar year since 2025) and the 20 h/week rule for non-EU students with a 'labour market limited' permit.
National interprofessional GMMI/RMMMG (CCT/cao no. 43); sector scales can be higher.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students staying more than 3 months: register as a student
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri che restano più di 3 mesi: registrazione come studente
items.summary: Register with the commune/gemeente where you live within three months of arriving. You get an Annex 19 (proof of application, showing your Belgian national number) and must hand in the supporting documents within three months of it; after a police address check you are invited to collect an electronic residence card (EU card).
steps: Book an appointment at the city office soon after arrival (Leuven: as soon as possible).

Bring ID card or passport, proof of enrolment (an admission letter is not enough), health insurance for the whole stay (preferably the EHIC; travel insurance is not accepted), a passport photo, a rental contract if you have one, and a signed declaration on honour of sufficient means.
Put your name on doorbell and letterbox for the police address check.
Wait for the e-mail invitation (up to 2 months in Leuven) and collect the residence card.
items.deadline: Apply within 3 months of arrival; documents within 3 months of the Annex 19 (late application: possible € 200 fine)
items.cost: Leuven: € 24 for the residence card appointment (2026); other communes set their own fee
items.authority: Commune/gemeente of residence; Immigration Office (FPS Home Affairs)
items.notes: Document list and fee are Leuven's; Ghent and Brussels city pages could not be read (403 / navigation only). Applies in all regions because residence law is federal.

items.title: EU/EEA citizens staying less than 3 months: report your presence
items.title_it: Cittadini UE/SEE che restano meno di 3 mesi: dichiarazione di presenza
items.summary: For a short stay, report to the commune where you stay shortly after arriving; you receive an Annex 3ter. Late reporting can bring an administrative fine of € 200. People staying in hotels or similar accommodation covered by guest-registration rules are exempt.

interpretations.hypothesis: The deadline is 10 calendar days after arrival (wording 'within 10 days of arriving').
The deadline is 10 working days (the same page uses '10 working days' where it describes the fine).

items.title: EU/EEA exchange (mobility) students up to 6 months, and border students
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE in scambio (mobilità) fino a 6 mesi e studenti frontalieri

applies_to.stay_duration: up to 6 months (mobility programme such as Erasmus)
other: Border-student option only for residents of the Netherlands, France, Germany or Luxembourg

items.summary: An EU/EEA student on a mobility programme of up to 6 months can report as a 'mobility student' and gets an Annex 3septies (max 6 months) instead of full registration: no Belgian national number, but a BIS number can be requested to work. Residents of NL/FR/DE/LU can instead report as border student (Annex 33, one academic year) or register in full.
items.deadline: As soon as possible after arrival
items.notes: Read on the City of Leuven pages; other communes apply the same federal annexes but their procedures were not checked. Exchange students staying longer than 6 months should register in full (be-residence-eu-long-stay).

items.title: Non-EU students: type D student visa and A-card
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: visto D per studio e carta A

other: Enrolled full-time at a recognised higher education institution, or in a preparatory year

items.summary: Apply for a long-stay type D visa at the Belgian embassy/consulate (passport, medical certificate, criminal-record certificate if 18+, fee, proof of enrolment, sufficient means, health insurance for the whole stay). Within 8 working days of arrival register at the commune, which issues a limited-period residence permit (A-card) valid up to one academic year plus one month, renewable.
steps: Apply for the D visa from your home country (fingerprints and photo taken).
Register at the commune within 8 working days of arrival (Leuven: your institution forwards your file; collect Annex 15 at the city office).
Police address check at your address.
Collect the A-card when invited (up to 2 months in Leuven).
Renew at the commune at least 15 days before expiry; renewal can be refused for insufficient study progress (e.g. bachelor: 45 credits in each of the first two years).
items.deadline: Register within 8 working days of arrival; renew at least 15 days before the card expires
items.cost: Visa: administrative fee (amount not stated on the page; scholarship holders of Belgian/EU authorities may be exempt). Leuven residence card: € 24 (2026)
items.notes: EU Immigration Portal page last updated 18 Sep 2025. The sufficient-means amount and visa fee are on the DOFI site, which was behind a captcha and could not be read; a search snippet of DOFI said 'within 8 days' (not working days) for registration, so advise students to register immediately. After studies, a stay can be extended up to 12 months to look for work or start a business.

items.title: Non-EU students coming on mobility from another EU country
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE in mobilità da un altro paese UE

other: Holds a valid student residence card of another EU country
Mobility notified by the Belgian institution

items.summary: If you already study in another EU country with a residence card there, your Belgian institution notifies your mobility; you then report to the city with passport, the other EU residence card, the mobility notification and a photo and receive an Annex 33 valid for the mobility period. You are not entered in the national register.
items.deadline: Book only after the city invites you; as soon as possible after arrival
items.notes: Non-EU exchange students coming directly from outside the EU for more than 90 days were not covered by a page we could read; check with the host university's international office.

items.title: Registration at the commune/gemeente and police address check
items.title_it: Iscrizione al comune (commune/gemeente) e controllo di residenza della polizia
items.summary: In all three regions, registration is done at the commune/gemeente where you live. EU/EEA citizens staying more than 3 months must apply within 3 months of arrival; non-EU students with a D visa within 8 working days. A local police officer then checks that you live at the address, so your name must be on the doorbell and letterbox.
items.deadline: EU/EEA: within 3 months; non-EU: within 8 working days of arrival

items.title: National register number (rijksregisternummer / numéro national) or BIS number
items.title_it: Numero di registro nazionale (rijksregisternummer / numéro national) o numero BIS
items.summary: Students who register in full are entered in the national register; for EU students the number is printed on the Annex 19. Mobility (Annex 3septies) and border students (Annex 33) get no national number but can request a BIS number if they want to work (e.g. to use Student@work).
items.authority: Commune/gemeente (national register); BIS register via the social-security Crossroads Bank
items.notes: The exact procedure for a student to request a BIS number was not found on an official page; usually the employer or the commune handles it.

items.title: EU/EEA students: EHIC, and free registration with a Belgian fund
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE: TEAM ed iscrizione gratuita a una mutua belga
items.summary: The EHIC is enough if it covers your whole stay: you get care at Belgian rates, pay upfront and are refunded (about 75%). For a longer stay KU Leuven advises registering with a local mutualité/ziekenfonds (free with an EHIC; CAAMI-HZIV charges no contribution) to get an ISI+ card. If your EHIC does not cover the full stay you need extra cover or must join a fund and pay.
items.cost: No contribution with a valid EHIC (2026)
items.notes: The EHIC does not cover repatriation, private care or planned treatment. Whether taking a Belgian job makes Belgian insurance mandatory was not found on an official page.

items.title: Non-EU students: join a Belgian health insurance fund
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: iscrizione obbligatoria a una mutua belga

other: Self-supporting, or scholarship without health insurance
Not covered by a bilateral agreement (e.g. Albania, Algeria, Australia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Morocco, Serbia, Montenegro, Tunisia, Turkey, UK)

items.summary: Health insurance is a condition of the student visa. To be covered by Belgian public insurance you join a Belgian fund as a 'student' and pay € 78.93 per quarter (2026) while waiting for your residence permit, plus a membership fee of about € 100–120/year (none at CAAMI-HZIV). Nationals of countries with a bilateral agreement should check with the fund first.
items.cost: € 78.93/quarter (2026) + € 100–120/year membership fee depending on the fund
items.notes: Once you hold a residence permit the contribution depends on income (KU Leuven page). Private insurance covering the stay is also accepted as proof for the visa.

items.title: Right to a basic payment account
items.title_it: Diritto a un conto di pagamento di base

other: Legally resident in an EU country

items.summary: Anyone legally resident in the EU is entitled to a basic payment account (card, transfers, deposits, withdrawals, no overdraft); a bank cannot refuse you just because you live in another EU country, though it can refuse on anti-money-laundering grounds. Fees must be reasonable and disclosed in advance.
items.cost: Set by the bank; annual fee must remain reasonable
items.authority: EU rules (Payment Accounts Directive), applied by Belgian banks
items.notes: No Belgian government page for consumers was found (FPS Economy's basic banking service page covers businesses). Universities have practical pages, e.g. https://www.kuleuven.be/english/life-at-ku-leuven/money-matters/bank-matters-and-currency-exchange (not read).

items.title: Student transport passes on the MOBIB card (De Lijn, STIB)
items.title_it: Abbonamenti per giovani sulla carta MOBIB (De Lijn, STIB)
items.summary: Transport is regional: De Lijn in Flanders (Leuven, Ghent), STIB-MIVB in Brussels, TEC in Wallonia (Louvain-la-Neuve). Passes are loaded on a MOBIB card; De Lijn charges € 10 administration for the MOBIB card. Youth rates depend on age (18–24) and, for STIB's cheapest pass, on living in the Brussels Region; see subsidies.json.
items.cost: De Lijn MOBIB card: € 10 administration fee

items.title: Student jobs: 650 hours per year with reduced contributions (Student@work)
items.title_it: Lavoro studentesco: 650 ore l'anno con contributi ridotti (Student@work)

other: Studying must be your main activity

items.summary: Since 1 January 2025 a student may work 650 hours per calendar year at reduced social contributions; from the 651st hour normal contributions apply. EU/EEA/Swiss students have the same rights as Belgian students. Check your remaining hours in My Student@work or the app. Graduating in June/summer, you may keep working as a student until 30 September.
items.authority: RSZ/ONSS (National Social Security Office) — Student@work; federal rule valid in all regions
items.notes: To use My Student@work you need a national register or BIS number. Students living in NL/LU/DE/FR who report as border students (Annex 33) pay at least 25% non-refundable tax (Ghent University job service: https://www.ugent.be/en/facilities/jobservice/overview.htm).

items.title: Non-EU students: 20 hours/week during term, no limit in holidays
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: 20 ore/settimana durante i corsi, senza limite nelle vacanze

other: Valid residence permit (A-card) or Annex 15 while waiting for it

items.summary: With a permit marked 'labour market limited' you may work up to 20 hours a week during the academic year and without limit during official school holidays; with an 'unlimited' permit you work under the same conditions as Belgian students. Work only while the permit is valid, outside class hours; arriving in summer, you cannot work before the academic year starts.
items.notes: The 20 h/week cap and the 650-hour reduced-contribution quota are separate rules. Whether a separate work permit is needed was not stated on these pages; UGent says the residence card must include the right to work.

items.title: National minimum wage (GMMI / RMMMG)
items.summary: The interprofessional guaranteed average minimum monthly income is € 2,233.61 gross/month full-time for workers aged 18+ from 1 July 2026 (pro rata for part-time). Sector scales set by joint committees can be higher. Students under 21 on a student contract can be paid a reduced percentage (cao/CCT no. 50).
items.authority: FPS Employment, Labour and Social Dialogue; National Labour Council (CNT/NAR)
items.notes: The CNT page still shows the earlier step (€ 2,189.81 from 1 April 2026); the July 2026 figure reflects a 2% indexation. Youth percentages per payroll provider Securex (not official): 90% at 20, 85% at 19, 79% at 18 on a student contract (https://www.securex.be/nl/lex4you/werkgever/actuele-bedragen/sociaalrechtelijke-bedragen/nationaal-gmmi).
